searchText: I haven't looked at the implementations yet, but has anyone done a fork choice that works from the known heads and traverses towards tail / parents instead of starting with justfitied and traversing towards heads / children? the reason being that it's inefficient to keep a children list - most of the time it will contain only the one child of the canonical chain, so it makes sense to keep a list of "known heads" and travers backwards from there of course, having a list of known heads makes it possible to build the childrens list should there be need - potentially pruning simple paths like <@!361447803194441738> & co did - but I wonder if that's even necessary? The proto_array fork choice I’ve been working on starts at the the heads and goes backwards I really like proto_array, I think it’s a very useful data structure perfect, writing code is so much easier when you don't have to think for yourself 🙂 Agreed! Unfortunately proto_array needs some thought to adapt to match the spec exactly Buuut, I’m presently doing that thought so you can steal it when I’m done! Looking forward to that <@!361447803194441738>! And this is where fork choice spec test will come in handy, to verify correctness of various optimizations When would you be available to cowork-call about fork-choice <@363800010518822915> <@361447803194441738> ? Looking forward to dive back into this. It has been 8 months (yes, wow) since I proposed that proto-array approach, and I'm interested in how it is being adapted for the current spec version, and where I can help. I'm flexible. You guys can choose and I'll be there I'm also flexible, this week would work for me. I'm moving house next week so it becomes a little more difficult. I'm also flexible, <@!361447803194441738> can pick a time, credits to him for reviving the fork-choice optimization Thanks proto! What's your timezone and morning/evening preference <@!363800010518822915>? same to <@!203220829473996800> 🙂 I'm PST. Preferably before Friday the 17th. I'll be out of office that day. 🙂
